rules_text:
Rules summary Overview Have the most gold twice Turn You always have 2 cards to choose from Place a card onto one end of the trail by overlapping one half with a half already present The half played and the half overlapped must match in colour If you cannot play a card, you are out for the round The new half which overlapped the old half has its effect triggered, NOT the half that hangs off Draw back to 2 cards at turn end Round End The round ends when the set number of draw deck depletions occur All treasure and remaining hand cards score, and the player with the most points wins the round If this was that player's second win, they win!

---

The objective of the game is to have the most accumulated gold by the end of the game among the players still in contention.

Turn Sequence
The active player plays a card from their hand onto the track.
They draw a card from the deck to replenish their hand to 2 cards.
End of turn. Change of active player in a clockwise direction.

To play a card, the active player MUST overlay one of their squares on one of the two ends of the track. To do so, they overlay the square on their card onto the selected end's square. Note: the associated square colors must match (except for multicolored squares).
Next, the active player applies, if possible, the effect of their overlaid square and ends their turn by replenishing their hand. It's then the next player's turn, proceeding clockwise, to begin their turn.

—description from the publisher

Dans la forêt de Nottingham, l’or du roi est transporté vers son château, mais le parcours ne se
fera pas sans encombre : de nombreux brigands sont cachés dans celle-ci. Nos chers gobelins
sont là eux aussi mais pour rendre l’or au pauvre peuple,...Ou pour le garder pour eux ?

But du jeu
Être le joueur ayant accumulé le plus d’or en fin
de partie parmi les joueurs toujours en lice.

Tour de jeu
Le joueur actif joue une carte de sa main sur
le parcours.
Il prend une carte de la pioche pour
compléter sa main à 2 cartes.
Fin de tour. Changement du joueur actif
dans le sens des aiguilles d’une montre.
Pour jouer une carte, le joueur actif DOIT super-
poser une de ses cases sur une des 2 extrémités
du parcours. Pour ce faire, il superpose la case de
sa carte sur celle de l’ extrémité sélectionnée.
Attention: les couleurs de cases associées
doivent correspondre (sauf les multicolores).

—description from the publisher (French)

[Rating: 1/10] Played on BGA.  Untested.  Game can be won 1st turn before 2nd player gets a move.

[Rating: 1/10] Seemed like a fun game until you find out the final rule of the game for when you can't play a card. How patently stupid of a game design. Quentin, you're awful.

[Rating: 3/10] Designer: Quentin Lammerant Playing time: 10-20 Min Weight: 1.50 / 5 Publisher: TwistGames Player count: 2-4 (best with: 2)  [b]COMPLEXITY: Low COMPONENTS: N/A DOWNTIME: Low FUN: Low INTERACTION: High PLAYING TIME: Low LUCK: High REPLAY VALUE: Medium SOLITAIRE: Very low THEMATIC: Very low[/b]  [b]Comments:[/b] [thing=411050][/thing] is an abstract family card game about hand management and take that. The ideia is that players will use their cards in order to match those already played on either side of the road - the color must match, and when a card is used, it triggers the effect on the side

[Rating: 3/10] Random and filled with luck from the draws. I didn't feel like I had any control whatsoever to what I would like to do on a turn. There's no need to play again.

[Rating: 3/10] Play a card (you may or may not have a choice here) and more often than not just do a thing that doesn't benefit you in any way. Basically dominos with cards and random effects.

[Rating: 3/10] I hate to pile on with the negative comments but this game is pretty much random.  What powers you can play, whether it is useful or not, what and how much treasure you end up with, there is very little player choice and sometimes you may not even have that.  I am trying very hard to think of anything good to say, but it honestly feels like a prototype that needs more work than a complete game.

[Rating: 4/10] Play a card and take an action. Simple, fast, incredibly luck driven. The different actions are not balanced and so drawing more of the better cards is... well.... better. If ultra light and fast card game play is what you are looking for then this is should be right up your alley, but I can't really see myself ever looking to play this game again.

[Rating: 4/10] Place cards on same colors, activate powers or get eliminated. Very lucky, not much game to it.
